scope: Independent test fixtures only; no production case selection or chess interpretation is keyed by these positions.

cases.purpose: An empty target loses one white controller while another white controller and the black controller remain.
The third occupant leaves a rook ray; the first and second occupants and the rook's actual control remain unchanged.
The first occupant leaves the same geometry as the preceding case, exposing the second occupant to direct control.

reference.context: Doknjas Najdorf, Hjartarson-Vidit, 22.Bf3; the narrow queen-support statement is an independently reconstructed board claim, not an attributed quotation.

cases.purpose: A bishop move opens the stationary queen's h2 support while the bishop's attack on the same d5 knight persists.

reference.context: Doknjas Najdorf, Zvara-Swiercz, 25.Bc3; board functions are checked independently below.

cases.purpose: The same bishop keeps two supports, loses another support and creates an attack, while also blocking a stationary queen and rook.
Moving a non-pawn creates both f-pawn routes; the g-pawn has only one route because its second destination is occupied.
A diagonally pinned starting-rank pawn has two clear forward routes and geometric controls, but neither advance is legal.
The pawn's clear routes cannot answer a rook check; after the king escapes, it is the opponent's turn, not a newly certified white legal-move inventory.
A pawn's diagonal capture opens the stationary rook's file and removes a different pawn; captures are not forward routes.
Legal en passant clears two squares of a horizontal ray although the move lands elsewhere; both stationary rooks gain mutual control.
The pawn geometrically controls the empty en-passant target and the right exists, but using it exposes the own king to a rook.
One empty forward destination permits four promotion moves; a separate capture destination permits four more. Underpromotion ends the pawn resource but not the physical actor.
